description.p: ohmail is an email client for the mailbox you already have. It connects to your own IMAP server over TLS, mirrors your mail to a database on this computer, and files new mail into ohmail/ folders on the server itself — where every other mail app you own can see it.

First-time senders wait in the Screener until you say where they belong. Nothing is filed out of your inbox before you have decided, and a decision you make here is a folder move on your server, so it is still true when you read the same mailbox on your phone.

The app carries its own mail engine and the runtime it runs on. Besides your mail server, it fetches the pictures in a message you open (a switch makes each message ask first), sends the one-click unsubscribe a screen-out asks for where the list offers one (a switch turns it off), looks up through your system's DNS resolver the key a company or a newsletter signs its mail with, where your provider does not confirm senders itself, and, only if you turn it on, sends requests to the model provider you chose. This build does not check for updates, because your software centre installs them.
It works with any IMAP account — your own server, a hosting provider, or a mailbox from a large provider that issues app passwords. There is no account to create to use it.

A letter deleted on the server leaves no preview behind, and a delete whose answer was lost stays in Trash
Desktop downloads always find a folder, Windows updates go in at the next start
The sender's address line keeps the name before the @ whole, and the proxy reads OHMAIL_TLS_TERMINATOR only as addresses
Sending says what happened, and Microsoft mailboxes keep one Sent copy
An unfinished first mailbox setup's password is no longer used
Look-alike link text gets its note, and a web PDF preview only ever opens in its worker
The phone previews pictures and PDFs, resumes a kept reply and deletes on its own
A search with "or" keeps the letters each word finds inside a longer word
A self-hosted server behind your own terminator needs OHMAIL_TLS_TERMINATOR set before you update
A letter your mail provider failed waits in the Screener for you to decide
Signing out reaches the server later when it cannot at once, and a recovery code confirms it is you
Three timing tests wait for events, not milliseconds
A sign-out, and a sign-in after one, end the previous session on the server
Erasing a mailbox takes the fingerprint of its saved settings too
ohmail clears out its own old settings copies that a mail server kept
Letters removed from Trash in another mail app leave ohmail's Trash
The phone keeps the letter you opened in Trash when a delete commits
Words you typed are kept when you quit, close, press Escape or reload
The desktop app keeps syncing after a mailbox is removed and connected again while it is closed
Shift+J, Shift+K and Shift-click select only the messages you step over, even after a read message
A minus word only leaves letters out of a search
A new search order starts at the top result again
